previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: An elderly male with a history of atrial fibrillation, COPD, CAD s/p CABG, and alcohol abuse was admitted after presenting with chest pain and found to be hypotensive with acute liver failure. Evaluation revealed markedly elevated transaminases and a positive acetaminophen level, consistent with hepatotoxicity exacerbated by recent heavy alcohol use. He was treated with N-acetylcysteine, antibiotics for right upper lobe pneumonia, and supportive care for alcohol withdrawal. His liver function improved, and he was transitioned to the floor before discharge to extended care. He was restarted on home medications, educated on avoiding alcohol and acetaminophen, and referred for outpatient follow-up in liver clinic, neurology, and psychiatry.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  CHEST (PORTABLE AP)

INDICATION:  History: ___ with dyspnea. Evaluate for pneumonia

TECHNIQUE:  Portable upright chest radiograph

COMPARISON:  ___

FINDINGS: 

There is extensive right upper, right lower, and left lower lobe consolidation
concerning for infection.  Aspiration is a strong likelihood given the nature
of the patient's presentation.  There is no associated pleural effusion.
Cardiomediastinal silhouette is normal.  No pneumothorax or pleural effusion.

IMPRESSION: 

Findings are concerning for multifocal pneumonia, right worse than left.

EXAMINATION:  CT HEAD W/O CONTRAST

INDICATION:  ___ male status post fall. Now with altered mental
status.

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous axial images of the brain were obtained without
contrast. Coronal and sagittal as well as thin bone-algorithm reconstructed
images were obtained.

DOSE:  DLP:  1206 mGy-cm
CTDI:  61 mGy

COMPARISON:   ___ noncontrast head CT

FINDINGS: 

There is no evidence of infarction, hemorrhage, edema, or mass.  Prominence of
the ventricles and sulci is indicative of volume loss. Moderate to severe
periventricular white matter hypodensities are nonspecific, likely sequela of
chronic small vessel ischemia. There is an unchanged area of encephalomalacia
in the right parietal-occipital cortex, compatible with prior infarct.
Atherosclerotic vascular calcifications are noted of bilateral cavernous
portions of internal carotid arteries.

Small right frontal scalp soft tissue swelling is noted, without underlying
fracture.  There is mild mucosal thickening of the anterior ethmoid air cells,
otherwise the paranasal sinuses, mastoid air cells, and middle ear cavities
are clear.

IMPRESSION:


1. Small right frontal scalp soft tissue swelling.
2. No evidence of acute intracranial hemorrhage or fracture.
3. Chronic right parietal-occipital infarct, unchanged compared to ___ prior exam.
4.  Atrophy, probable small vessel ischemic changes, and atherosclerotic
vascular disease as described.

EXAMINATION:  CT C-SPINE W/O CONTRAST

INDICATION:  ___ male status post fall, now with altered mental
status. Evaluate for cervical spine fracture.

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous axial images were obtained.  Sagittal and coronal
reformatted images were generated.  No contrast was administered.

DOSE:  CTDIvol:  846 mGy
DLP:  37 mGy-cm

COMPARISON:  ___ cervical spine CT.

FINDINGS: 

Alignment is normal.  No fractures are identified. There is again noted T1
vertebral body bone island. No evidence of severe central canal narrowing. 
Grossly stable multilevel degenerative changes noted throughout the cervical
spine.  Imaged lung apices demonstrate extensive opacification in the right
lung, better evaluated on the concurrent CT of the torso.  Atherosclerotic
vascular calcifications are noted throughout bilateral cervical vertebral
arteries and common carotid artery bifurcations. There is minimal right
sphenoid sinus mucosal thickening.

IMPRESSION:


1. No evidence of fracture or malalignment.
2. Multilevel degenerative changes, grossly stable compared to ___
prior CT cervical spine study.
3. Atherosclerotic vascular calcifications as described.
4. Minimal paranasal sinus disease as described.
5.  Please see concurrently obtained head CT study with accession ___ for
description of cranial structures, and CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis
with accession ___ for description of non cervical structures.

EXAMINATION:  CT CHEST/ABD/PELVIS W/O CONTRAST

INDICATION:  History: ___ with fall, altered mental status. Evaluate for solid
organ injury and fractures.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT images were obtained from the thoracic inlet to the pubic
symphysis without intravenous contrast.  Axial images were interpreted in
conjunction with coronal and sagittal reformats.

DLP:  1056 mGy-cm
CTDIvol:  16 mGy

COMPARISON:  CTA of the chest from ___ and CT of the torso from
___.

FINDINGS: 

CHEST: There is a patulous fluid-filled esophagus to the level of the thoracic
inlet, which predispose the patient to aspiration.  The distal esophagus is
thick walled, possibly indicating esophagitis.  There is moderate
atherosclerotic calcification of the aortic arch and great vessels, without
aneurysm formation. Descending thoracic aorta demonstrates moderate
calcification as well. The heart is normal in size with scattered coronary
artery calcifications but no pericardial effusion. Right lower paratracheal
lymph node (03:10) measures 12 mm. Several other right lower paratracheal
lymph nodes demonstrate pathologic enlargement, for example (03:17), measuring
13 mm, and enlarged subcarinal and bilateral hilar lymph nodes.
There is extensive airspace opacification throughout the right lung, which is
superimposed upon mild to moderate centrilobular emphysema and fibrotic
changes, demonstrated at the left lung base (03:41). Trace pleural effusion is
noted on the right. There is no rib fracture or evidence of traumatic injury
to the chest.

ABDOMEN:
Evaluation of the intra-abdominal solid organs is limited by lack of
intravenous contrast.
The liver is hypoattenuating, compatible with fatty infiltration. The
gallbladder contains large gallstones near the neck, but is decompressed. The
pancreas demonstrates significant lipomatosis with no surrounding stranding.
Spleen is normal in size and attenuation. The adrenal glands are normal
bilaterally. The kidneys demonstrate cortical hypodensities bilaterally,
likely representing cysts. There is no hydronephrosis.
The stomach contains a large amount of fluid. The small bowel is decompressed.
The appendix is normal. Ascending colonic and sigmoid colonic diverticula are
noted, without diverticulitis. There is no mesenteric or retroperitoneal
lymphadenopathy, or intra-abdominal free air or free fluid.

PELVIS: The urinary bladder, prostate, and seminal vesicles are unremarkable.
There is a moderate amount of stool in the rectal vault. There is no pelvic
free fluid or lymphadenopathy.

VESSELS: The aorta demonstrates moderate atherosclerotic calcification without
aneurysmal dilatation. Central venous catheter enters the right femoral vein
and terminates in the right external iliac vein.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES: No evidence of fracture in the chest, abdomen, or pelvis. 
No soft tissue hematoma is appreciated.  There is generalized osteopenia.

IMPRESSION: 

1. Extensive opacification in the right lung, superimposed upon emphysema and
chronic fibrotic changes, compatible with pneumonia. Significant mediastinal
and hilar lymphadenopathy is presumed to be reactive, however follow up after
completion of treatment is recommended to ensure resolution.
2. Patulous, fluid-filled esophagus to the level of the thoracic inlet,
predisposes the patient for aspiration. Consider aspiration pneumonia as an
etiology for the pulmonary consolidation.  Thickened distal esophagus could
represent esophagitis, but warrants evaluation with endoscopy to exclude
neoplasm.
3.  Hepatic steatosis.
4. Chronic findings including atherosclerotic calcification of the coronary
arteries, aorta, and iliac vessels, cholelithiasis without cholecystitis,
bilateral renal hypodensities, and diverticulosis without diverticulitis.

RECOMMENDATION  Thickened distal esophagus could represent esophagitis, but
warrants evaluation with endoscopy to exclude neoplasm. Significant
mediastinal and hilar lymphadenopathy is presumed to be reactive, however
follow up after completion of treatment is recommended to ensure resolution.
